papers.title_en: VLG-Drive: Unifying Vision-Language and Geometric Priors for Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Junge Zhang, Jie Zhu, Yanqi Jia, Xiangyu Xu, Zixun Huang, Wenbin He, Xin Li, Jiachen Li, Liu Ren
papers.evidence: 融合视觉语言语义与几何先验的纯相机端到端规划器
papers.tldr: 自动驾驶规划同时需要场景语义与空间结构，但视觉语言模型和几何基础模型各自只提供其中一部分。VLG-Drive 将这两个模型都冻结，仅训练融合接口与规划器：在每个相机网格单元，用几何锚定的残差把配对的 VLM 特征与几何特征融合成联合 token，再由命令条件规划器据此预测自车轨迹。在 NavHard 扰动初始状态下取得 31.78 EPDMS（对比方法中最高），仅用相机在 NavTest 上达到 88.27 PDMS，点式融合优于独立双流，420 个 HUGSIM 闭环场景中也优于所有对比规划器。这表明轻量规划器加冻结基础模型的融合特征，是替代微调任一模型做规划的有效方案。
papers.abstract_en: A driving planner needs both scene semantics, which vision-language models (VLMs) provide, and spatial structure, which geometric foundation models recover from visual history. We present VLG-Drive, which keeps both models frozen and trains only a fusion interface and a planner from trajectory labels. At each camera-grid cell, the interface fuses the paired VLM and geometry features into one joint token through a geometry-anchored residual, and a command-conditioned planner reads these tokens to predict the ego trajectory. VLG-Drive achieves 31.78 EPDMS on NavHard under perturbed initial states, the highest among the compared methods, and 88.27 PDMS on NavTest from cameras alone. Pointwise fusion outperforms independent VLM and geometry streams on both benchmarks. In closed-loop driving on 420 HUGSIM scenarios, VLG-Drive outperforms all compared planners. These results indicate that a lightweight planner trained on fused features of frozen vision-language and geometric foundation models is an effective alternative to adapting either model for planning.

papers.title_en: Commit2Drive: Perception-Grounded Language Decisions as Commitments for Trajectory Planning in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
papers.authors: Zikai Zhang, Hubert P. Shum, Toby Breckon
papers.evidence: 视觉-语言-动作端到端驾驶模型，用语言决策约束轨迹规划
papers.tldr: 现有VLA驾驶模型的语言决策与轨迹常不一致，且语言标注未与轨迹核验。Commit2Drive把语言决策定义为带连续参数的机动承诺，经Maneuver Bank映射为运动学代码，并以一致性损失约束轨迹执行；其自动数据管线用专家未来运动、反事实执行和VLM生成并精炼监督。在Bench2Drive上，该方法以0.5B模型取得DS 78.50、SR 55.91%，可在单张消费级显卡上在线闭环推理，显著降低语言-动作不一致。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models introduce language reasoning into end-to-end autonomous driving. They output a language decision together with a trajectory, which makes the planner more interpretable. However, in existing methods the language decision is either an independent output or an index that selects among similar candidate trajectories, and its annotations are not verified against the trajectory. As a result, the language decision and the trajectory are often inconsistent in closed-loop driving. To address this, we propose Commit2Drive, a framework that imposes the language decision as a consistency constraint on trajectory planning. The decision is a commitment, a maneuver class with a continuous parameter that one deterministic rule reads from any trajectory, and it is grounded in facts reported by the perception of the model itself. A Maneuver Bank maps the commitment to a code with a kinematic meaning, and consistency losses train the planner to execute every admissible decision of a scene, so that the trajectory follows the decision. An automatic data pipeline supplies the supervision. Decisions are labeled from the future motion of the expert, counterfactual executions train the decision and the trajectory together, and rule-based functions with a Vision-Language Model (VLM) generate, review and refine the language annotations. The code is a lookup that involves no hidden state of the language model, so Commit2Drive is extensible to rule-based decisions, which the same planner executes without retraining. Commit2Drive uses a 0.5B language model and runs closed-loop inference online on a single consumer graphics card. On Bench2Drive, Commit2Drive reaches a Driving Score (DS) of 78.50 and a Success Rate (SR) of 55.91% with a lightweight model, which is competitive with the state of the art, and greatly reduces the language-action inconsistency. Code will be released soon.

papers.title_en: Attention Is Not Relevance: Challenging the Causality of Attention in Autonomous Driving
papers.evidence: 用反事实方法检验注意力是否反映驾驶决策中的因果对象相关性
papers.tldr: 注意力被广泛用于判断自动驾驶中周围物体对决策的相关性，但其是否反映因果关系仍存疑。本文以PlanT 2.0为基础，在超过8万条合成驾驶场景中，将多种基于注意力的相关性估计方法与反事实分析得到的因果参考进行对比。结果显示注意力只体现相关性而非因果性，在单车道直道场景较准确，但在多车道与交叉路口等复杂场景明显退化。该工作揭示了注意力作为物体相关性代理的局限，呼吁开发能准确捕捉单个物体因果影响的新方法。
papers.abstract_en: Attention has become one of the most widely adopted solutions for estimating the relevance of surrounding objects and interpreting an autonomous vehicle's driving decisions. However, its ability to capture the causal impact of individual input elements on an AI model's output has long been discussed in the literature, particularly in the Natural Language Processing (NLP) domain. This work brings this discussion into the autonomous driving domain by analyzing the accuracy of attention in estimating the impact of an input object on an autonomous vehicle's driving, i.e., its relevance. To this end, we compare different attention-based relevance estimation methods against a causal reference of object relevance obtained through counterfactual analysis. We perform our analysis on more than 80,000 synthetic driving scenes using an autonomous vehicle based on PlanT 2.0, a state-of-the-art Transformer-based model for object-level planning. Results show that attention provides a correlational rather than causal indication of object relevance. Attention-based relevance estimation methods do not consistently identify all relevant objects and tend to incorrectly classify as relevant objects with little or no impact on the vehicle's driving. In particular, results show that attention can effectively identify relevant objects in simple single-lane, straight-road scenarios, but its accuracy degrades in more complex settings, such as multi-lane roads and intersections. These findings highlight the limitations of attention as a proxy for object relevance, calling for novel methods able to accurately capture the causal impact of individual objects on the vehicle's driving and distinguish it from correlational associations.

papers.title_en: Imagine Smarter, Drive Faster: Efficient World Modeling for Decision-Aware Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Feiyang Jia, Lin Liu, Zhicheng Bao, Caiyan Jia, Ziying Song, Shengkai Zhang, Lina Han, Yan Zhao, Xiaoshuai Hao
papers.evidence: 面向未来感知自动驾驶规划的轻量世界模型
papers.tldr: 自动驾驶世界模型虽能辅助规划，但想象未来的计算代价高，现有蒸馏与领域预训练又把负担转移给教师或训练流程。FastWorld 提出原生轻量世界模型，通过紧凑场景表示、短时程动作条件预测，以及选择性候选验证与分数精炼来降低计算。它在单张 4090 上于 NAVSIMv1 达 92.2 PDMS、132 FPS，并在 NAVSIMv2 与 nuScenes 取得有竞争力结果。该工作证明无需教师蒸馏或额外领域预训练，也能实现高效且面向决策的未来感知规划。
papers.abstract_en: World models hold great promise for autonomous driving planning, yet their ability to imagine the future often comes at a formidable computational cost. Efficiency efforts, such as knowledge distillation and domain-specific pre-training, often shift this burden to costly teachers or training pipelines, leaving lightweight world modeling an open challenge. We introduce FastWorld, a natively lightweight world-model framework for efficient autonomous driving planning. FastWorld reduces computation through compact scene representations, short-horizon action-conditioned prediction, and selective candidate verification and score refinement. These designs support efficient future-informed planning without teacher distillation or additional domain-specific pre-training. On NAVSIMv1, FastWorld achieves 92.2 PDMS at 132 FPS on a single 4090 GPU. It also achieves 89.4 EPDMS on NAVSIMv2 and an average L2 of 0.40 over 3 seconds at 17 FPS on nuScenes. Code and models can be found at https://github.com/MoyangSensei/FastWorld.

papers.title_en: AXE: AlpaSim E2E Closed Loop Challenge Technical Report
papers.authors: Joonhee Lim, Seonmyeong Lee, Sihwan Hwang, Hanbin Jang, Hiwon Shin, Dogun Kim, Hyelin Jo, Hyeonjun Jeong, Yongjae Lee, Junseong Kwak, Junhyeok Park, Satyam Mishra, Juyeb Shin, Uisung Kim, Hyeonseo Kim, Saparkhan Kassymbekov, Hailemichael Molla Gashaw, Abi Rahman Syamil, Mingyu Kim, Hyeongjun Kim, Yeina Lee, Moogeun Park, Dongsuk Kum
papers.evidence: 从传感器到规划的端到端自动驾驶闭环流程
papers.tldr: 针对闭环端到端自动驾驶的安全需求，本文构建涵盖数据整理、HD地图自动标注、模仿学习与仿真强化学习的完整流水线。核心是引入基于选择的E2E规划：利用目标检测和BEV分割过滤易碰撞或驶出道路的轨迹候选，并按碰撞、可行驶区域合规与进度对固定候选集评分。方法在NVIDIA NuRec和PAI-AV数据上训练，从模拟rollout学习评分并选出通过过滤的最佳轨迹。该工作表明E2E规划与感知轨迹过滤结合可提升闭环驾驶的安全性与可靠性。
papers.abstract_en: This report presents a comprehensive pipeline for developing an end-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving model for the Physical AI AV Track. The framework consists of data curation, HD map auto-labelling, data-driven imitation learning, and simulator-based reinforcement learning. To ensure safety in the closed-loop setting, we introduce a selection-based E2E planning approach that leverages object detection and BEV segmentation to filter out trajectory candidates likely to cause collisions or off-road driving. Trained on NVIDIA NuRec and the NVIDIA PAI-AV dataset, our method scores a fixed vocabulary of trajectory candidates for collision, drivable-area compliance, and progress learned from simulated rollouts, and selects the best candidate that passes the filter. This design highlights the effectiveness of combining E2E planning with perception-based trajectory filtering for safe and reliable closed-loop autonomous driving.

papers.title_en: GeoTex: Geometry-as-Texture Encoding and History-Grounded 4D Occupancy Forecasting
papers.authors: Shijun Guo, Yaming Yang, Haoran Xu, Wei Zhao, Ziyu Guan, Cai Xu, Peixi Peng
papers.evidence: 面向驾驶世界模型的几何感知4D占据预测
papers.tldr: 4D占用预测需建模三维场景演化，但现有语义占用压缩时弱化列内高度模式与列间关系，且预测阶段未充分利用历史观测。GeoTex将几何视为纹理，联合编码列内高度模式与列间关系为紧凑潜表示，并通过内容依赖高度展开与几何交互恢复结构。预测端用固定跨观测关系记忆保留初始证据，并以目标参考残差更新引入近期历史，后接仅解码器适配。相比GenieDrive，平均预测mIoU和IoU分别提升9.79%和11.91%，参数量由3.47M降至2.33M，长时程增益更明显。
papers.abstract_en: 4D occupancy forecasting models 3D scene evolution to support future prediction and scenario generation in autonomous-driving world models. Semantic occupancy abstracts image color and texture into discrete labels, leaving 3D voxel arrangements as the primary cues for distinguishing local shapes within each class. Existing methods borrow image-encoding frameworks to obtain compact latent representations through height channelization or plane factorization, but do not sufficiently model within-column height patterns and cross-column relations jointly before compression, weakening these geometric cues. Forecasting also underutilizes complementary history and struggles to retain reliable observation evidence. We therefore propose GeoTex, an occupancy world model combining geometry-as-texture encoding with history-grounded forecasting. GeoTex Representation jointly encodes within-column height patterns and cross-column relations into compact continuous latent representations and restores 3D structure through content-dependent height unfolding and geometric interaction. GeoTex Prediction retains initial evidence throughout rollout in fixed cross-observation relational memory and incorporates complementary recent history through target-referenced residual updates. After prediction training, decoder-only adaptation improves semantic decoding of predicted states. GeoTex improves average forecasting mIoU and IoU by 9.79% and 11.91% relative to GenieDrive while reducing parameters from 3.47M to 2.33M, with gains increasing at longer horizons. Code is included in the supplementary material.
